AI Business Mentor

A thinking partner for founders, freelancers and side projects. It asks the questions a good mentor would ask and helps you turn a vague idea into numbers and next steps.

TL;DR
  • Best for testing an idea, setting prices and planning the next 90 days.
  • Give it real numbers: costs, prices, customers, hours you have.
  • Use it to prepare, then check big decisions with people who know your market.

What this coach helps with

  • Checking whether an idea can make money before you spend on it
  • Setting and testing prices
  • Finding your first 10 customers
  • Planning a 90-day roadmap
  • Preparing for a meeting with a partner, investor or bank

Prompts you can copy

Copy a prompt, paste it into the Zehn AI Chat or any AI assistant, and replace the parts in [brackets] with your own details.

  1. Act as my business mentor. My idea is [idea]. Ask me 5 hard questions an experienced founder would ask before I spend any money.

  2. I sell [product] for [price]. My costs per unit are [costs]. Work out my margin and how many sales a month I need to cover [fixed costs].

  3. Give me 3 cheap ways to test demand for [idea] in the next 14 days, with what result would count as a yes.

  4. Who exactly is my first customer for [product]? Describe 3 specific types of people and where I can find each of them.

  5. Write a 90-day plan for [business] with one goal per month and the three tasks that matter most each week.

  6. I have [hours] hours a week and [budget] to spend. What should I stop doing so I can focus on what grows [business]?

  7. Play a sceptical investor. I will pitch [business] in 5 sentences; tear it apart politely, then tell me what to fix.

  8. Compare these two options for my business: [option A] and [option B]. Make a table of cost, risk, time and upside.

  9. My sales dropped from [number] to [number] in [period]. List the most likely causes and how to check each one this week.

  10. Write a short, honest message to my first 20 potential customers about [product] that does not sound like an ad.

  11. Help me price [service]. Ask about my time, my costs and my clients, then suggest three price levels with what each includes.

  12. Summarise our chat as a one-page plan: goal, numbers, risks, and the first three actions with deadlines.

Two example conversations

Written by the Intellect AI team to show the style of answers. Not a real user conversation.

ExamplePricing a home-baking side business

YouI bake cakes at home and charge $25 each. Friends say it's too cheap. Ingredients cost about $9 and each cake takes me 3 hours.

Business MentorThen you earn about $5 an hour for your time, before packaging and delivery. Let's test a new price: $38 for the standard cake and $55 for a custom one. Before changing anything, which three recent customers would you ask whether they'd still order at $38?

ExampleChoosing between two ideas

YouI can either open a small phone-repair stall or start a repair course online. I have $3,000.

Business MentorThe stall gives you cash flow quickly but ties you to one place. The course scales but needs an audience you may not have yet. A cheap test: run a weekend repair stall for one month and record five short repair videos. Whichever gets real demand first wins your $3,000.

Tips for better answers

  • Share numbers, not adjectives. “30 customers, $12 average order” gets a far better answer than “sales are slow”.
  • Ask it to argue against your idea. The objections are usually more useful than the praise.
  • Keep one chat per project so the mentor remembers the context.
  • Finish with a dated action list and review it with the coach a week later.

Questions people ask

Can an AI business mentor replace a real mentor?

Not completely. An AI mentor is fast, patient and available at any hour, which makes it great for preparing, testing ideas and doing the maths. A human mentor brings contacts, local market knowledge and lived mistakes. Use the AI to arrive at every human conversation with sharper questions and clearer numbers.

What should I tell the business mentor first?

Start with what you sell, who buys it, your price, your monthly costs and how much time and money you have. Then say what you want: a pricing check, a plan or a list of risks. The more concrete the facts, the less generic the advice you get back.

Is it safe to share business details with an AI chat?

Share what you need to get a useful answer, but leave out passwords, bank details, private customer data and anything under a confidentiality agreement. Describe customers in general terms instead of by name. Treat the chat like a conversation with a smart stranger: helpful, but not the place for secrets.

Does the AI know my local market?

Only partly. AI models learned from a lot of public text, so they know general business patterns well, but local prices, rules and trends may be missing or out of date. Ask the mentor what you should verify locally, then check those points with real customers, suppliers or an accountant.
